from slugs import slugify


def test_precomposed_accents_transliterate():
    assert slugify("Caf\u00e9 d\u00e9j\u00e0 vu") == "cafe-deja-vu"


def test_decomposed_accents_match_precomposed():
    decomposed = "cafe\u0301 de\u0301ja\u0300 vu"
    assert slugify(decomposed) == "cafe-deja-vu"
    assert slugify(decomposed) == slugify("Caf\u00e9 d\u00e9j\u00e0 vu")


def test_ascii_word_separation_preserved():
    assert slugify("Hello, World!") == "hello-world"
    assert slugify("foo   bar") == "foo-bar"


def test_dashes_trimmed():
    assert slugify("  --Caf\u00e9--  ") == "cafe"
    assert slugify("") == ""


def test_result_is_ascii_str():
    result = slugify("Caf\u00e9 d\u00e9j\u00e0 vu")
    assert isinstance(result, str)
    assert result.isascii()

patches.rationale: The current slugify lowercases then strips non-[a-z0-9] runs, so accented characters are simply deleted (e.g. 'café' -> 'caf', 'déjà' -> 'd-j'). The issue requires transliterating Unicode combining accents to their ASCII base letters before slug generation, so precomposed 'é' and decomposed 'e' + U+0301 both yield 'e'. I'll normalize with NFKD, drop combining marks (category Mn), then apply the existing lowercase/replace/strip logic. This preserves ASCII word separation and dash trimming, and keeps the existing contract (Hello, World! -> hello-world, '' -> '').
